questions.explanation: Variance is the expected squared deviation from the mean: $\operatorname{Var}(X)=E[(X-E[X])^2]$.

questions.question: Why is standard deviation often easier to interpret than variance?

It has the same units as the random variable
It is a probability between zero and one
questions.explanation: Standard deviation is in the SAME units as $X$ (variance is in squared units), so it is easier to interpret.

option_explanations: It is not always equal to the mean.

Standard deviation is $\sigma_X=\sqrt{E[(X-E[X])^2]}$, the root-mean-square deviation from the mean, so it directly quantifies spread in the units of $X$; variance uses squared units, which is why it is harder to read.
It is not a probability in $[0,1]$.
